overview_pre: This page is a **reference for dermatological terms**: how to describe lesions precisely so that a description alone points to a diagnosis.
kf: Describe: **site, number, distribution, configuration, size, shape, colour, surface, palpation** (SCALP-style).
Primary lesions: macule/patch (flat), papule/plaque (raised, solid), nodule (deep), vesicle/bulla (fluid), pustule (pus), wheal (transient oedema).
Secondary changes: scale, crust, erosion, ulcer, excoriation, lichenification, atrophy, scar.
Configurations: annular, linear (Koebner, Blaschko), grouped (herpetiform), target, reticulate, serpiginous.
Size thresholds: macule/papule under 1 cm (some use 0.5 cm); vesicle under 0.5 cm vs bulla.
patho_lead: Each primary lesion reflects **what sits at which depth** of the skin.

mech.t: Macules and patches are colour change only; papules, plaques and nodules are solid and raised, deeper as they grow.
mech.cap: Primary lesions in profile: macule, papule, plaque, nodule, vesicle and pustule.

mech.t: Vesicles and bullae hold clear fluid; pustules hold pus.

myths: **"Rash" is a description**: precise terms change the differential diagnosis.
